Status: planned, wave 3; repositories not created yet, one per algorithm family, names not fixed.
Clustering, classification and model selection in pure Go (PLAN.md item 15, wave 3). The bibliography sizes the work as XL and proposes splitting it per algorithm, so the repository layout is not fixed.
No code exists yet: nothing on this page is released, measured or tested. It says what the library is planned to provide and how it will be checked. The wave and the order are in PLAN.md; the state of each item in STATUS.md.
data.how-it-will-be-validated#How it will be:
Reference tools are run as oracles, driven from Go by exec with JSON on a pipe; the unit suite must pass with no oracle installed.
Oracle How scikit-learn, statsmodels uv run --with scikit-learn --with statsmodels; JSON in, JSON out UCI Machine Learning Repository https://archive.ics.uci.edu (iris, wine, digits); per-dataset licences to check What “correct” means:
Area Criterion Clustering and classification deterministic given a seed: partitions exact against scikit-learn with the same initialisation; adjusted Rand index equal to 1 on a shared init Accuracy within cross-validation noise of the oracle
data.reference-implementations#Reference impl: Implementation Licence and use scikit-learn (Python/Cython) BSD-3-Clause; port permitted: k-means, DBSCAN, trees, forests, GMM LIBSVM, LIBLINEAR (C/C++) BSD-3-Clause; port permitted: SVM and logistic regression malaschitz/randomForest (Go) Apache-2.0; a reuse candidate golearn (Go) MIT; inspect only, last push 2024-01

data.risks-and-open-questions#Risks and open: Linear algebra is the bottleneck: PCA, SVM and GMM need QR, Cholesky and symmetric eigen solvers tested to LAPACK accuracy; check what go-ndarray and gonum provide before sizing. Corpus licences (UCI datasets) must be checked per file; prefer download-on-demand into a directory outside the repositories. The name go-learn is taken, so the organisation is go-mlkit.
data.what-it-will-provide#What it will provid: Clustering k-means (Lloyd, k-means++ seeding), hierarchical clustering, DBSCAN, Gaussian mixtures by EM Dimension reduction PCA, factor analysis and rotations Classification logistic regression, SVM (SMO and dual coordinate descent), decision trees, random forests, gradient boosting, k-NN Model selection cross-validation splitters, grid search, metrics (accuracy, ARI and others) Neural networks deferred, priority 3: nn on top of go-autodiff’s reverse mode, outside the first scope
